title: Streams
lede: Two stream worlds live here. The WHATWG classes (ReadableStream/WritableStream/TransformStream, plus Compression/Decompression) run on the promise/microtask runtime alone — no fibers or libcurl for in-memory pipelines. Node's stream module (Readable/Writable/Duplex/Transform/PassThrough, pipeline/finished, duplexPair) is Node v24's own implementation ported to TypeScript and compiled with the program, so its event order follows Node's. The recurring divergences: a synchronously-throwing pull/start/write of a web stream propagates to the caller instead of erroring the stream, an array/tuple-chunk closed-stream read still yields a zero-shaped value rather than undefined, an omitted error argument to a Node stream callback arrives as null rather than undefined, and fs/http hand out their own stream handles rather than instances of the Node classes.

entries.name: ReadableStream
entries.description: A pull/push source with backpressure: enqueue via a controller in start/pull, consume with for await, .getReader().read(), or by piping. ReadableStream.from() builds one from an array. Runs on the promise/microtask runtime alone — no fibers or libcurl for in-memory pipelines.
differences: No BYOB readers / byte controllers (`type: 'bytes'` rejected at compile time) — byte data flows as `Uint8Array` chunks through default readers
`ReadableStream.from()` accepts arrays only, not async iterables
Source callbacks must be arrow/function-expression/method-shorthand literals; a cancel callback can't take a reason parameter

`read()` on a closed stream whose chunk type is an **array/tuple** still yields the chunk's zero-shaped value, not `undefined` (an array slot has no spare absent state); a scalar/string/object chunk reads a real `undefined`, and `controller.desiredSize` is `null` once errored
`releaseLock()` leaves queued pending reads pending instead of rejecting them
`values()` returns a reader usable in `for await` only (no standalone `.next()`)
In the no-fiber tier, `await` of an already-settled `read()` skips the microtask drain, so a pending pull can run one tick later than real JS
A synchronously-throwing pull/start propagates to the caller instead of erroring the stream
`tee()` forwards the last cancelling branch's reason instead of composing both; a signal abort of `pipeTo` takes effect at the next chunk boundary

entries.name: WritableStream
entries.description: A backpressured sink: .write() queues a chunk (each write carries its own promise), .close()/.abort() finish it, and ready re-arms on backpressure flips. The sink's write/close/abort callbacks drive delivery.
differences: `releaseLock()` doesn't reject a pending-write view
A synchronously-throwing sink write propagates instead of erroring the stream (an async rejection is handled per spec)
A sink abort callback can't take a reason parameter; no transformer/sink `start` promise-vs-write interlock beyond the started flag

entries.name: TransformStream
entries.description: A writable-in / readable-out pair whose transform callback maps chunks from one side to the other, running when the readable side has capacity (else parking one chunk). Compose it with pipeThrough. Writable HWM defaults to 1, readable HWM to 0.
differences: No transformer `start` callback
Cancelling the readable side doesn't error the writable side
An identity transform (no callback) requires matching I/O chunk representations

entries.name: CompressionStream / DecompressionStream
entries.signature: new CompressionStream(format): TransformStream; new DecompressionStream(format): TransformStream
entries.description: TransformStreams backed by native zlib: gzip/deflate/deflate-raw compress and decompress a Uint8Array chunk stream. Inflate auto-detects gzip/zlib wrappers, and -lz is linked only when one of these is actually constructed.
differences: The format argument must be a string literal ("gzip", "deflate", "deflate-raw") — a runtime-computed format string is a compile error
Chunks are `Uint8Array` only (no ArrayBuffer/DataView BufferSource variants)

entries.name: Blob.stream()
entries.description: Returns a ReadableStream<Uint8Array> over the blob's bytes — one owned-copy chunk then closed (an empty blob yields no chunk). Consumable via for await or .getReader().

returns.desc: A readable stream of the blob's bytes.

differences: Delivers the blob's bytes as a **single** `Uint8Array` chunk (the whole blob), not incrementally chunked as a real byte source would be

entries.name: stream.Readable / .Writable / .Duplex / .Transform / .PassThrough
entries.signature: new Readable({ read() { this.push(chunk) } }); class X extends Writable { _write(chunk, encoding, callback) {} }
entries.description: Node's stream classes, ported from Node v24's own implementation to TypeScript and compiled with the program: the same states, event order and process.nextTick deferrals. The options form binds this to the stream, subclasses override _read/_write/_transform/_final/_destroy, chunks are Buffers (or strings with setEncoding, or any value in object mode), and Readable.from/.toWeb/.fromWeb bridge to arrays and web streams.
differences: An omitted error argument reaches a callback declared `(err?: Error | null)` as `null`; Node passes `undefined`
`Readable.from` takes an array, a string or a Buffer; a generator or other iterable is not supported
The fs streams and the HTTP server's `req`/`res` are separate runtime handles, not instances of these classes
`Readable.toWeb` has no pull backpressure; `Duplex.toWeb`/`fromWeb` are missing
Not ported: `compose`, `addAbortSignal`, the readable operators (`map`/`filter`/`toArray`/…), `Readable.wrap`, `Duplex.from`, `isReadable`/`isErrored`/`setDefaultHighWaterMark`, the `signal` option
A method replaced on an instance (`this._read = fn`) is not supported; pass it in the options

entries.name: stream.pipeline() / .finished()
entries.description: The callback forms: pipeline(a, ...b, cb) pipes each stream into the next and calls cb once the last has finished, or with the first error, destroying every stream; finished(s, [options,] cb) calls cb when the stream has ended, finished and closed, and returns a function removing its listeners. Their promise twins live in stream/promises.

returns.desc: pipeline returns the last stream; finished returns its cleanup function.

entries.snippet:
finished(echo, (err) => { console.log("echo finished, clean:", !err) })
pipeline(src, new PassThrough(), sink, (err) => { console.log("pipeline done", err ? err.message : "ok") })
differences: Function stages (`pipeline(src, async function* …)`) and the `signal` option are not supported — every stage is a stream

entries.name: stream/promises
entries.description: The promise-returning pipeline and finished, over the callback forms: pipeline resolves once the last stream has finished, finished once the stream has ended and closed; either rejects with the stream's error.

returns.desc: Resolves on completion, rejects on error.

entries.snippet:
import { pipeline, finished } from 'stream/promises'
await pipeline(numbers, square, sink)
await finished(words)

entries.name: stream.duplexPair()
entries.description: Two Duplex instances wired to each other: what one side writes, the other reads. A write completes when the peer reads it, and end() finishes once the peer has ended, as Node's DuplexSide does. Returned as a two-element array.

returns.desc: A pair of cross-wired Duplex streams.
